finalOutput:
The game is complete. **`snake_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html`** (600 lines, ~19 KB) was created as a single self-contained file — HTML + CSS + JS, no external dependencies.

## What was built

**Core game (30×30 grid, 600×600 canvas, 20px cells)**
- Snakes move continuously on a fixed-step loop (~100 ms/tick via `requestAnimationFrame` accumulator)
- Eating food grows the snake and respawns food on a free cell; **hitting a wall or any snake body ends the game**
- Simultaneous two-snake step with correct tail-vacating semantics: a cell the tail leaves this tick is passable, and head-to-head collisions kill both snakes (draw)

**Three game modes** (selectable in the start menu via ↑/↓ + Enter/Space, or hot-keys 1/2/3 to start instantly):
1. **Human vs Human** — P1: arrow keys · P2: WASD
2. **CPU vs Human** — P1 is CPU; the human (P2) can use *both* WASD and arrows
3. **CPU vs CPU** — spectate two AIs

**CPU AI** ("automatically searches for food"): each tick it evaluates all non-reversing directions, filters out moves into occupied cells (tails excluded since they vacate), then scores candidates by flood-fill reachable-space (avoids self-trapping dead ends), Manhattan distance to food, a penalty for cells adjacent to the opponent's head (avoids head-ons), and a small bonus for keeping its current direction.

**UI & flow**
- **HUD** above the canvas: live P1/P2 scores with color chips + current mode name
- **Start menu** overlay: title, mode list with highlighted selection, controls legend
- **Game over** overlay: winner ("Player 1 wins!" / "Player 2 wins!" / "Draw!"), final scores
- **Restart with a keypress**: `R` or `Enter`/`Space` restarts the current mode (from game over or mid-game); `M` returns to the menu; arrow/space key page-scroll is prevented
- Dark modern styling: gradient background, glowing canvas, rounded snake segments with directional eyes, pulsing food, kbd-styled key hints

Open the file directly in any browser to play.

{"path":"snake_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW self-contained HTML5 file (HTML + CSS + JS in one file, no external resources, works offline) implementing a two-snake battle game on a 30x30 grid. All code comments and UI text in English. The file must be complete and run without console errors in a modern browser.

PAGE STRUCTURE
- <!DOCTYPE html>, <html lang="en">, <head> with meta charset + viewport, <title>Snake — Battle Arena</title>, one <style> block.
- Body: centered layout. A .hud bar ABOVE the canvas, a .stage container (position:relative, 600x600) holding <canvas id="game" width="600" height="600"> plus two absolutely-positioned overlay divs (#menu, #gameover, both initially hidden except menu), and a small #hint line BELOW the stage.

CSS (dark modern theme)
- body: min-height:100vh; flex center; background: linear-gradient(135deg,#0b1220,#111f38,#0b1220); color:#e2e8f0; system font stack.
- .hud: flex, spaced; two score chips (colored dot + "P1"/"P2" + score number) and a centered mode label.
- canvas: background #0d1526; border:1px solid #223; border-radius:10px; box-shadow soft cyan glow.
- Overlays: absolute inset 0, flex column center, background rgba(8,12,22,.85), backdrop-filter blur(3px), rounded corners, text-align center.
- .mode-option list items; .selected state with bright border/background highlight. <kbd> styled key chips. .hidden { display:none }.
- Title "SNAKE" large, bold, gradient text (background-clip:text).

GAME LOGIC (single <script> at end of body)
Constants: COLS=30, ROWS=30, CELL=20, STEP_MS=100.
Direction map DIRS with {dx,dy} and opposites.
Game state machine: 'menu' | 'playing' | 'over'.
Modes array: [{id:'hvh',label:'Human vs Human',p1:'human',p2:'human'}, {id:'cvh',label:'CPU vs Human',p1:'cpu',p2:'human'}, {id:'cvc',label:'CPU vs CPU',p1:'cpu',p2:'cpu'}]. Menu selection index 0..2.

Snakes: two objects {body:[{x,y},...] head first, dir, pendingDir, alive, score, isCpu}. Spawn: P1 head at (6,15) moving right (body extends left, length 3), P2 head at (23,15) moving left (length 3). One shared food item on a random free cell (never on any snake segment); if no free cell exists → end game, winner by higher score (practically unreachable).

Main loop: requestAnimationFrame with a time accumulator; one simulation step per STEP_MS. render() every frame (for food pulse animation).

Step logic (both snakes move simultaneously):
1. For each alive snake resolve direction: humans use pendingDir (ignored if it is the exact opposite of current dir); CPU uses AI (below).
2. Compute newHead for each alive snake; eating = newHead equals food cell (head-to-head on food is impossible because heads coincide → death).
3. Build preview occupancy per snake: its current segments MINUS the tail cell when it is not eating (tail vacates this tick).
4. Deaths: (a) newHead out of 0..29 bounds; (b) newHead in own preview cells; (c) if both new heads are equal → BOTH die; (d) newHead inside the OTHER snake's preview cells (its head cell excluded — covered by (c)).
5. Apply for survivors: unshift newHead; if eating → score++ and spawnFood(); else pop tail. Dead snakes stop moving (rendered gray).
6. If any snake died → state 'over', show game-over overlay; winner = the surviving snake, or draw if none/both died.

CPU AI (aiChooseDir(snake, other)): candidates = 4 directions except reverse of current dir. Build occupied set = union of both snake bodies minus own tail (approximation of tail vacating). Safe candidates = target in bounds and not occupied. If none safe → keep current dir (will die). Score each safe candidate: flood-fill BFS free-space count from the candidate cell (treat occupied as blocked, cap at 120 expansions) weighted heavily (avoid self-trapping), minus Manhattan distance to food (go get it), small penalty if the cell is orthogonally adjacent to the opponent's head (avoid head-on), tiny bonus for continuing straight (less jitter). Pick the highest score. (In CPU vs Human mode P1 is the CPU, P2 is the human; in CPU vs CPU both are CPU.)

Rendering per frame: clear; subtle grid lines (or faint checker); food as a pulsing red circle (#ef4444) with a darker rim, radius oscillates via performance.now(); each snake: segments as rounded rects (implement a small manual rounded-rect path helper — do NOT rely on ctx.roundRect), body color slightly transparent toward tail, head brighter with two white eye dots offset by current direction. P1 = green (#3ddc84), P2 = orange (#ff9f43). Dead snake drawn desaturated gray. HUD score numbers and mode label updated every frame.

INPUT (window keydown; preventDefault for Arrow keys and Space to stop page scrolling):
- state 'menu': ArrowUp/ArrowDown (and w/s) move the highlighted mode option (wrapping); digit keys 1/2/3 immediately select and START that mode; Enter or Space starts the selected mode.
- state 'playing': in 'hvh' Arrow keys steer P1 and W/A/S/D steer P2; in 'cvh' BOTH arrow keys and WASD steer the human P2 (P1 is CPU); in 'cvc' movement keys are ignored. R restarts the current mode instantly; M returns to the menu.
- state 'over': Enter, Space, or R restarts the same mode; M returns to the menu.

UI CONTENT
- Menu overlay: title "SNAKE", tagline, the three mode options (showing which snake is CPU where relevant), controls legend: "P1: Arrow Keys · P2: W A S D · R: Restart · M: Menu", and "Press Enter / Space to start".
- HUD: "P1" chip + score, mode label center, "P2" chip + score.
- Game-over overlay: winner headline ("Player 1 wins!", "Player 2 wins!", or "Draw!") colored by winner, final score line (e.g. "P1 12 — 8 P2"), and "Press Enter / R to play again · M for menu".
- Hint line under canvas: "P1: ↑ ← ↓ →   ·   P2: W A S D   ·   R Restart   ·   M Menu".

QUALITY: valid HTML5, clean structured JS with comments, no external fonts/libraries/images, no syntax errors, no console errors."}
